title: Keep the science plain beside a personified story
statement: When a story personifies a natural process, keep the informational text paired with it in plain mechanism language, and make the difference between them explicit.
detail: A grade-4 geology unit's misconception guards, drawn from cross-subject science guidance, reject agentive language such as the Earth being angry and let literary texts personify, but require the informational texts to keep mechanism language clean, with the pairing making the difference explicit. Its language rule separates observation ('the ground shook') from mechanism ('plates slipped'). A body unit's pairing of a literal and a figurative text must likewise mark which sense is in play, so that the pairing teaches the distinction instead of risking the misconception.

evidence.quote: Watch personification in disaster narratives — literary texts may personify, but the informational spine must keep mechanism language clean, and the pairing must make the difference explicit.
distinguish observation ("the ground shook") from mechanism ("plates slipped") — don't let narrative texts blur them.
the pairing is the vehicle for teaching the distinction, not a misconception risk, provided the marking is taught.
